newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends with gains on weather.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends with gains on weather.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended higher across the board Tuesday in moderate trade, driven by forecasts for colder weather next week for the eastern half of the nation, industry sources said.
March climbed 18.4 cents to close at $2.497 per million British thermal units. April settled 16.2 cents higher at $2.269. Other deferreds ended up by 3.1 to 11.6 cents.

"The market might have been a little oversold and got spooked by the (cold) weather. Obviously, there's still some concern about the remains of winter and we may be done probing the downside for a while," said one Houston-based trader.

Revised forecasts for much-below normal Midwest weather next week plus normal to below-normal expectations for the East and South helped trigger some short covering today after the recent slide. But with eastern storage at a comfortable year-on-year surplus that is likely to grow more in the next two weeks, few expected the rally to be sustained unless the cold lingers.
Early withdrawal estimates for Wednesday's weekly American Gas Association storage report range from 150-180 bcf compared to a 213 bcf decline in the same week last year.
Technically, traders pegged March resistance at $2.50 and then in the $2.70 and $2.80 area. Trendline support was seen in the $2.30 area and then at the November 5 low of $2.12.
In the cash, Gulf Coast prices gained 10 cents Tuesday to the mid-to-high $2.50s. Midcon pipes also were up a dime or more to the low-to-mid $2.40s.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip gained 8.8 cents to $2.24. NYMEX said an estimated 30,656 Hub contracts traded, up from Monday's revised tally of 22,319.
NYMEX Alberta and Permian natgas did not trade Tuesday.
On the KCBT, March finished 14.5 cents higher at $2.20, while deferreds ended up by 2.5 to eight cents. The East/West spread widened by 3.9 cents to 29.7 cents (NYMEX premium).
